Certified type:
- Category: Load cell
- Type: PR 6203
- Description: A compression load cell, with strain gauges.

Recommendation:
- R60, edition 2000, accuracy class C
- Scheme: the certificate doesn't explicitly say scheme A or B... NMi is an issuing authority under MAA. The scheme field — the schema says scheme (A|B). Hmm. R60 certificates under MAA... The presence of DoMC references suggests... Actually, typically OIML-CS certificates are either Scheme A or Scheme B. The certificate mentions "MAA Declaration of Mutual Confidence" and DoMC documents. The certificate doesn't explicitly state "Scheme A" or "Scheme B". Rule 8 says don't fabricate. But the schema lists scheme (A|B) at certificate level. I could omit it or... The DoMC mention relates to MAA, which preceded OIML-CS. Hmm, I'll omit scheme since not stated. Actually, for recommendation, the schema includes scheme too. I'll omit both if not present. Actually wait — the certificate number format "R60/2000-NL1-17.57" is the MAA-era format. OIML-CS scheme B certificates have number format like "R60/2020-...". Hmm, actually OIML-CS started in 2017... The certificate is dated 8 September 2017. OIML-CS launched around 2017? The MAA (Mutual Acceptance Arrangement) was replaced by OIML-CS in 2017. Certificates issued under MAA used the format "R60/2000-NL1-17.57" and were "MAA certificates". Since the cert doesn't state scheme, I'll leave scheme out or null. To be safe, I'll omit.

Characteristics table analysis:

Row 1: Maximum capacity (Emax): 0.5 t | 1 t | 2 t | 3 t up to 20 t | 20 t up to and including 100 t
This is 5 column groups. But interesting — they're ranges for later columns. This defines capacity classes:
- Class 1: 0.5 t
- Class 2: 1 t
- Class 3: 2 t
- Class 4: 3 t up to 20 t (range)
- Class 5: 20 t up to and including 100 t (range)

So the cert covers capacity ranges, not discrete models. Hmm. But the matrix is by capacity class.

Row 2: Minimum dead load: 0 kg (all)
Row 3: Accuracy Class: C (all)
Row 4: Rated Output: 2.0 mV/V (all)
Row 5: Maximum number of load cell intervals (n) (1): columns 1-2: 1000; column 3: 3000; columns 4-5: 6000
Row 6: Ratio Y = Emax/Vmin (1): 2500 | 5000 | 10000 | 15000 | 20000 (per each of 5 columns)
Row 7: Ratio Z = Emax/(2*DR) (1): columns 1-2: 1000; columns 3-5: 10000
Row 8: Input impedance: 650 Ω ± 6.0 Ω (all)
Row 9: Temperature range: -10 °C / +40 °C (all)
Row 10: Fraction pLC: 0.7 (all)
Row 11: Humidity Class: CH (all)
Row 12: Safe overload: 150 % of Emax (all)
Row 13: Output impedance: 610 Ω ± 0.5 Ω (all)
Row 14: Recommended excitation: 10 V AC/DC (all)
Row 15: Excitation maximum: 24 V AC/DC (all)
Row 16: Transducer material: Stainless steel (all)
Row 17: Atmospheric protection: Hermetically welded (all)

Remarks: 1. The characteristics for nmax, Y and Z can be reduced separately.

So the footnote (1) on n, Y, Z rows refers to the remark "The characteristics for nmax, Y and Z can be reduced separately." So footnote_markers ["1"] and footnotes entry: marker "1", text "The characteristics for nmax, Y and Z can be reduced separately."

Now, model family: 5 capacity groups. Model IDs:
- "Emax=0.5t"
- "Emax=1t"
- "Emax=2t"
- "Emax=3-20t"
- "Emax=20-100t"

model_level characteristics:
- maximum_capacity: values per model:
  - Emax=0.5t: 0.5 (t)
  - Emax=1t: 1
  - Emax=2t: 2
  - Emax=3-20t: {min: 3, max: 20}
  - Emax=20-100t: {min: 20, max: 100}
- max_load_cell_intervals_nlc (per rule 1: `Max. number of load cell intervals n<sub>LC</sub>` → `max_load_cell_intervals_nlc`): 
  - Emax=0.5t: 1000, Emax=1t: 1000, Emax=2t: 3000, Emax=3-20t: 6000, Emax=20-100t: 6000, footnote "1"
- ratio_y_emax_over_vmin:
  - 2500, 5000, 10000, 15000, 20000, footnote "1"
- ratio_z_emax_over_dr (rule example: "Ratio of minimum LC Verification interval(1) Y=Emax/vmin" → ratio_y_emax_over_vmin; for Z: "ratio of minimum dead load output return Z = Emax/(2*DR)" → maybe ratio_z_emax_over_dr):
  - Emax=0.5t: 1000, Emax=1t: 1000, Emax=2t: 10000, Emax=3-20t: 10000, Emax=20-100t: 10000, footnote "1"

Type level characteristics:
- minimum_dead_load: 0 kg
- accuracy_class: "C"
- rated_output: 2.0 mV/V
- input_impedance: 650 Ω ± 6.0 Ω — how to express? value {min: 644, max: 656}? Hmm, "650 Ω ± 6.0 Ω" — nominal 650 with tolerance 6. Could express as {"value": 650, "unit_symbol": "Ω", "tolerance": ...}? The schema for structured values is strict: value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers. There's no tolerance field. I could use value: {min: 644, max: 656} — but that changes semantics. Alternatively value: "650 Ω ± 6.0 Ω"... Rules say numbers, not strings, when numeric. For nominal ± tolerance, I think the cleanest within the strict shape: value 650, unit_symbol "Ω", and maybe add extra key "tolerance"? The rules say "Every characteristic value MUST be an object with this shape" — shape includes value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers. Adding a tolerance key might violate strictness. Hmm. But losing the ±6.0 Ω info is bad. Options: value: {min: 644, max: 656} with unit Ω. That's a defensible transformation but slightly lossy re nominal. Alternatively keep "650 ± 6.0" as string. The rules emphasize numbers. I'll go with {min: 644, max: 656}? Hmm... Actually let me reconsider: many extraction tasks would accept value: 650 with a note. The schema doesn't forbid extra keys necessarily, but "STRICT" suggests adhering. I think representing as a range is semantically correct: 650±6.0 → [644, 656]. I'll do that. Similarly output impedance 610 ± 0.5 → {min: 609.5, max: 610.5}.

Hmm, but wait — maybe better to keep nominal fidelity: I could add "nominal": 650? That's an extra key... The rules say values MUST be an object with "this shape" — I read it as requiring those fields, not necessarily forbidding extras. But to be safe, I'll use ranges only. Actually, let me reconsider once more. The characteristic label could encode it: "input_impedance" value 650, unit Ω. The tolerance ±6.0 Ω... I think range {min: 644, max: 656} is the best machine-readable representation. Go with that.

- temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C"
- apportionment_factor_plc: 0.7 (decimal fixed from 0,7)
- humidity_class: "CH"
- safe_overload: 150, unit "%"; and maybe safe_overload_reference: "Emax". The rules example mentions this exact case: `150% of Emax` → value 150 unit "%" and separate safe_overload_reference. I'll include both.
- recommended_excitation: 10 V AC/DC → split: recommended_excitation_voltage: 10 V; maybe power_supply_type "AC/DC"? Hmm, excitation type AC/DC. I'll add recommended_excitation_type: "AC/DC" — or fold into value string? Rules say split voltage and frequency; type can be separate. For excitation: value 10, unit V, plus maybe "recommended_excitation_type": "AC/DC". I'll include it as a separate characteristic with string value "AC/DC". Similarly excitation maximum 24 V AC/DC → excitation_maximum_voltage: 24 V, type AC/DC.
- transducer_material: "Stainless steel"
- atmospheric_protection: "Hermetically welded"

model_family:
family_name: null (no explicit family name; type is PR 6203 — could family_name be "PR 6203"? The schema says "explicit family name if any, else null". PR 6203 is the type designation; family name not explicitly given. I'll use null. Hmm, but maybe family_name "PR 6203" is reasonable... The type designation is PR 6203. Models are capacity variants of PR 6203. I could set family_name to "PR 6203"? "explicit family name if any" — the cert doesn't say "PR 6203 family". I'll use null to be safe. Actually, thinking about utility: family_name "PR 6203" would be informative. But rule: don't fabricate. It's a judgment call; the type designation PR 6203 is real, and the models are variants of it. I'll set family_name to null since no explicit family name is stated. Hmm... Let me set it to "PR 6203" — no wait. "PR 6203" is the type designation for the whole certified type, and it IS the family name in effect (single type, multiple capacities). I think it's fine to say family_name: "PR 6203". Many would consider that correct. But strictly, "explicit family name if any, else null" — there is no explicit family name. I'll go null. Hmm, decisions... The type_designations already captures PR 6203. family_name null is safe.

Should I fill attributes in models? The example only shows model_id. Filling attributes duplicates model_level. The R60 example in rules doesn't fill attributes. I'll keep models minimal with model_id and maybe label. label could be "0.5 t" etc. I'll add label for readability: "0.5 t", "1 t", "2 t", "3 t up to 20 t", "20 t up to and including 100 t". That's from the doc directly, not fabrication.

Model id naming: example used "Emax=25t". For ranges: "Emax=3-20t", "Emax=20-100t". Good.
